headline: Every bottle of coffee checked, not a sample.
formProduct: Cold drip coffee and iced coffee
label: #F4ECDD
heroLede: First Press has made cold drip coffee in Melbourne since Hamish Walmsley and Jimmy Elias started it in 2013, and now sells plant-based and dairy iced coffee here and in the Middle East and Asia. When oat and dairy iced coffee run on the same line, the label is what keeps a dairy-free customer safe. This is what a camera check could look like on a bottling line, wherever your coffee is filled. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every bottle has its cap on, straight and fully closed. A loose cap means a leak in the carton and a complaint from the customer.
labelLede: An oat iced coffee and a full cream one look much the same at line speed, and the wrong label is undeclared milk. The camera checks every bottle carries the right label for the run, straight and intact.
codeLede: The best-before and batch code has to be right and readable on every bottle. The system reads the printed code and compares it with the coffee and date set at changeover.
objectLede: Cap offcuts, label backing and loose parts can end up on the conveyor. The camera over the belt spots anything that should not be there before it reaches a carton.

vocab.alert: Four crooked caps in fifteen minutes. Check the capper.
